text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A new age begins after the secularist government wins a confidence vote in parliament, consigning the former Islamist-led coalition to history.
- The minister responsible for mining is to visit the site of a gold mine in western Turkey where locals have put up stiff opposition against the mine operators.
- Parliament erupts in chaos after a leftist deputy displays a banner attacking a controversial Islamist MP during the vote of confidence.
- The Capital Markets Board begins a probe into a group of companies suspected of collecting money illegally after a previous move to freeze assets of an Islamist holding.
- Conservative opposition leader Tansu Ciller vows to make a comeback after the collapse of her troubled coalition with Islamists.
- Foreign tourism officials say the tourist sector in Turkey would be finished if the Islamists returned to power.
- A leftist deputy prime minister puts forward plans for the country's privatisation process.
- A senior military official has yet to explain his alleged links with a security scandal which emerged last November.
- The Islamist financial sector's earnings amount to around $15 billion annually according to the secularist armed forces.
- The stock market is continuing steady gains after the appointment of the secularist government.
- A draft law on lifting the immunity from prosecution of deputies is ready to be presented to parliament after the new government won the confidence vote.
